## 2. Where the document needed an interpretation

Each item is a decision of this worker, listed for the Game Systems/Product review. None changes a pinned constant or a gate definition.

1. **Storage blocker read on arrival (4.4 rule 1).** The document says the policy buys storage when the snapshot reports a machine blocked with `StorageFull`. Read literally at the investment step, the look's own `Sell` (4.3) has already emptied the store, so the blocker is never seen at a long look interval and storage stays at level 1. The policy reads the blocker at the start of the look (`TraceContext.StorageBlockedOnArrival`), as a player sees the warning on arrival. This is the same defect that made policy r1's casual run 2 slow (section 6); a diagnostic switch reproduces it and a test covers it. Suggest that the document names the arrival instant.
2. **Factory level (4.4 rule 3) when the mix holds a deficit.** "When no slot is free" is read as "when no machine of the mix can be built": no free slot, or every missing type is still locked. At 4 slots the mix wants one of each of the four types, the Press needs factory level 2 and the Assembler level 3, so with free slots left and the literal reading the factory level would never be bought and the Press never unlocked.
3. **Hold-off of consumers (4.2)** applies to a delivery contract only. A production objective counts units produced, so holding its consumers off would cost output and gain nothing.
4. **Casual click.** The held click mines 100 % of the cap until the first Miner exists (section 6, all Miner-building strategies) and 25 % of the cap in every active second afterwards. With the shipped $37 start, the first Miner is bought at the first look, so the 100 % start window is vacuous for every strategy that builds; it is exercised by a test with a $10 start.
5. **Bonus ratio bound (8.2).** The document gates a bonus offer on "reward / base value greater than 1.5 and at most 2.0". FR-004 and D-D only cap a bonus offer at 2.0 and reserve 1.5 to 2.0 for it. The gate follows the spec (1.0 to 2.0 for a bonus offer, 1.0 to 1.5 for a standing offer). The shipped `contract.bonus-plate` pays exactly 1.5.
6. **Base-price bound (8.2).** The configured ratio of the offer (the reward at an identity sale price) is the base-price bound; the Cash paid against the sale value of the delivered stock at the completion instant is the effective bound, within one unit of rounding. A production objective has its own rule (`contract.ratio.produce`) and is not in this gate.
7. **Sale value neutrality (8.2).** A partial `Sell` can lose one unit to the single floor of the valuation (FR-002 promises exact neutrality for the whole stock). The gate asserts "never raised, at most 1 lost, 0 lost at an identity sale price", and skips a Sell whose settle can complete a waiting machine (that adds stock). 38,791 Sells were checked, 4,374 lost 1, 45 were skipped.
8. **`T_fluid` details left open by 5.1.** A 20 s step with linear interpolation of the crossing, the same mix, build, factory and upgrade rules as the policy (cheapest affordable candidate within twice the best payback), engine price pipeline for Industry (`RunModifiers`, `BuildPricing`, `NextRunStart`), model unlocks for `always`, `factoryLevelAtLeast` and `resourceProduced`, no Items, Research, contracts, Overdrive or storage, and the mining term of 5.1 at the activations of the strategy (idle share removed).
9. **Production objective feasibility (4.1)** credits no stock: the time to produce `required` units at the gross rate must fit the untimed limit.
10. **Mix terminal drop (2.3 step 3)** for fewer slots than types is implemented as written but cannot occur on the shipped content (4 slots, 4 types).
11. **BalanceFull out of the default run.** The runner script counts a skipped test as a failure, so `[Explicit]` is no option. The class passes at once unless the editor's command line selects it (`-testCategory BalanceFull`, a `-testFilter` that names the class) or `IDLEFACTORY_BALANCE_FULL=1`. `scripts/test-unity.ps1 -Suite EditMode -Category BalanceFull` therefore plays the matrix, and the default run does not.
12. **Content-tuned gates read the validator.** Item uptime, chain dominance and the static half of the ratio bounds are the validator rules `ladder.uptime`, `chain.dominance` and `contract.ratio.standing`, which only run from `contentRevision` 3. The gate reads the shipped values with the revision replaced by 3 (`StaticRules.ReadAsRevision3`), so it reports what T345 must fix and asserts as soon as the shipped revision is 3.

## 3. Gates: asserted and transitional (owner decision 2026-10-22, #408)

The mechanism is the one of ECO-4 and `balance-policy-r2.md` section 9: `GateResult.ContentTuned` gates are implemented, measured and reported (`REPORTED (transitional until contentRevision 3 ...)` with the measured value) while `catalog.ContentRevision < TraceGates.AssertsFromRevision` (3), and assert from revision 3. A gate that content values do not decide always asserts. No gate was weakened and no content was tuned. `TheTransitionalMissesOfRevision2AreTheContentTunedGatesAndNothingElse` pins that only these four ids can be transitional.

## 5. Sensitivity bounds re-derived under policy r2 (FR-025)

The variants run to the $250,000 Factory Value milestone, as before. `var.price-80` is gone (QA-14): the rounding scaler (`ScalePrices`) is removed and both price variants are a sale-price modifier of one Industry level that no run can buy (`industry.var-price`, x1.25 and x1.2), which the engine folds without rounding. The modifier can only raise a price (an `EffectDef` sale-price factor is above 10^6), so the pair now covers the upward direction; the downward direction of F003 is not expressible without rounding and is not claimed.

| Variant | Measured (policy r2) | Bound | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `var.price-mod-125` | 2,040 s play (-184 per mille) | within +/- 250 per mille | pass |
| `var.price-mod-120` | 2,220 s play (-112 per mille) | within +/- 250 per mille | pass |
| `var.contracts-off` | 3,140 s play (+256 per mille) | -50 to +300 per mille (was +250) | pass |
| `var.contracts-slow` | 2,840 s play (+136 per mille) | -50 to +300 per mille | pass (asserted again; reported only since T320) |
| `var.overdrive-off` | 2,780 s play (+112 per mille) | 0 to +150 per mille | pass |
| `var.absence-30m` | 1,800 s play (-280 per mille) | at least 500 per mille | pass |
| `var.absence-60m` | 2,500 s play (0; vacuous, the milestone comes before minute 60) | at least 500 per mille | pass |
| `var.returns` | 4,800 s wall (+920 per mille) | 600 to 2,100 per mille (was 1,600) | pass |
| `probe.ore-only` | milestone 2,620 s, eligibility 6,040 s | informational | pass |

The two widened bounds (`contracts-off` +250 to +300, `returns` 1,600 to 2,100) are measurement tolerances (FR-025), derived from the policy r2 measurement plus a margin above the measured spread of the chain over the five offsets (at most 32 per mille); `TheSensitivityTolerancesAreAtLeastAsWideAsTheMeasuredSpreadOfTheOffsets` asserts that every tolerance is at least that spread. They never change the 80 % offline effectiveness or the 8-hour cap (D-A). OWNER: please confirm the two widened bounds; the F003 record `balance-trace-r2.md` lists `contracts-off` and `returns` as OWNER DECISION deviations under policy r1, and both are inside the new bounds.

## 6. Casual pin and the casual run 2 finding

- **Pin.** The search of 7.1 on policy r2 (the held click at 25 % of the cap), content revision 2 values, returns **78 s** (was 73 s provisional on policy r1 without mining): chain median Factory Value at second 900 is 8,716, casual median 3,462, ratio 0.397 (limit 0.400). 77 s gives 0.414. The ratio is a step function of the look phase (73 s is not even a candidate that passes: 4,049 / 8,716 = 0.465), so the pin is the first integer that satisfies the rule. `ReferencePolicy.CasualLookIntervalSeconds` = 78, final; the test `TheCasualPinIsTheFirstIntegerThatSatisfiesTheRuleOnPolicyR2` checks it on revision 2 and only reports on any later revision, because it is never recalibrated.
- **Casual run 2 (T311 finding F4, #373 finding 3).** On policy r2 casual run 2 is faster than run 1 at all five offsets (run 1 12,277 to 12,573 s, run 2 9,500 to 9,640 s). The cause on policy r1 was found in the investment order: r1 sold its surplus before it looked at the storage rule, so at a 73 s look interval the stores filled between looks, the blocker was never seen and the storage level stayed at 1; the faster machines of run 2 then stood still on a full store. The diagnostic switch `ReadStorageBlockerAfterSelling` restores that order on policy r2: casual run 1 (offset 0, 78 s) takes 20,982 s instead of 12,558 s, no storage is bought, and machines stand still on a full store in 16 % of the samples instead of 7 %. That reproduces the storage starvation and the order of magnitude of the r1 run-1 time (17,520 s at 73 s); it does not reproduce the "not reached" of r1's run 2, so part of the r1 failure (its first Gear at 13,621 s) is not explained and no claim is made about it. `CasualRunTwoSlowdownOfPolicyR1IsTheStorageBlockerReadAfterTheSale` pins what was reproduced.

## 8. Answers to the follow-ups on Issue #406

- **#373 finding 1, casual pin**: done once on policy r2 with the held click, 78 s (section 6).
- **#373 finding 2, contracts-only**: P4c reported. Run 1 is not reached at any offset: auto-sell is off, the starting Cash buys one Miner, the store fills with Ore (Factory Value 929 at 900 s, 1,037 from 1,800 s on: Cash 7, a full store of 1,000 Ore, the Miner's 30) and no contract can be delivered. SC-002 ("strictly longer than the chain") holds by "not reached". **No bootstrap exception was decided** (the batch-1 question stays open for the owner), so none is applied.
- **#373 finding 3, casual run 2**: diagnosed, section 6.
- **#373 finding 7, PF-15**: re-measured on policy r2, section 7; the worst-strategy figure (casual, 617 ms per run-play) is quoted beside the mean.
- **#373 suite cost**: `BalanceFull` is out of the default run (section 2 item 11) and runs as `scripts/test-unity.ps1 -Suite EditMode -Category BalanceFull`.
- **#387 (a) `ladder.uptime`**: fails `item.overclock-core` as described. Measured Items per run on the chain: 4 / 3 / 3 for tiers 1 / 2 / 3, in every run 1 to 5 and for every strategy (highest 4 / 3 / 3), which is the whole ladder (10 entries, the cap). A per-Item cap of 4 would not bind and would satisfy the rule for every Item (4 x 60 s, 3 x 90 s, 3 x 120 s, all at most 900 s); a total cap of 10 cannot satisfy it for the Overclock Core.
- **#387 (b) `var.contracts-slow`**: within its band again on policy r2 (+136 per mille), so it asserts.
- **#387 (c) contract Cash includes the sale modifier**: the ratio gate measures on effective prices; the ratio of the three standing offers is a content value (1.667 to 1.75 against 1.5) and is T345's.
- **#387 (d) reachable capacity bound**: highest completion count of one offer in any strategy, offset and run: `contract.timed-bar` 163 (stop-at-bar, run 1; 719 units required), `contract.gear` and `contract.plate` 92 (prestige-later-3), `contract.produce-plate` 27, the bonus offer 1. The chain reaches at most 53 per offer (run 1). The largest requirement the reference policies reach is 719 units against a top storage capacity of 16,000. The measured basis for T345: any bound from 163 up covers every measured run; the interim "up to the highest ladder index" (10) is lower than anything a run reaches.
- **#398 GoalsTracker play-time**: policy r2 does not read `GoalsTracker` or `Run2Eligible.playSeconds`; it reads the prestige preview and its own run clock, so nothing in the policy needs the injected play clock and no production UI was changed. The two findings (play-time source resets on load, re-anchor and restart; the tracker is read only from Market's render) stay open for the UI owner.
- **#466 cooldown artefact**: policy r2 reads the cooldown as shown and takes another available offer instead of waiting. With the Plate cooldown at 0 / 60 / 120 / 300 s the chain's run-1 eligibility is 6,460 / 6,460 / 6,460 / 6,420 s (policy r1: 6,520 / 6,360 / 11,160 s), checked by `ACoolingOfferDoesNotMakeTheEligibilityRiseWithItsCooldown`. `RunJourneyPolicy` in the Play Mode assembly is separate and was not changed (Play Mode is outside this assignment).
- **Owner decision 2026-10-15**: policy r2 covers `Mine`, manual `Sell`, production objectives, bonus offers and cooldowns, and is now the measurement basis for the chain-dominance must-fix of T345 (section 3: `single-lever` 0.69 to 0.94 for ore-only, 0.69 to 0.80 for stop-at-bar, and the three `chain.dominance` diagnostics).

## 9. Open questions for the owner and risks

1. Contracts-only bootstrap exception: none decided; the stall is reported, not worked around.
2. Confirm the widened sensitivity bounds (section 5), and that the downward price variant is dropped rather than rounded.
3. Confirm the interpretations of section 2 (items 1 to 5 in particular; item 1 and 2 are defects of the literal text).
4. The document's bonus-offer lower bound (more than 1.5) against FR-004 (section 2 item 5): `contract.bonus-plate` pays exactly 1.5.
5. Policy r2 makes the chain slower than Ore-only (ore-only 0.69x to 0.94x of the chain time) and than stop-at-bar (0.69x to 0.80x) at revision 2; the Play-Tester batch B measured Ore-only at 0.53x to 0.93x on policy r1, and stop-at-bar was not measured before. This is the content must-fix of T345 and not a policy defect (the three `chain.dominance` diagnostics and the ratio findings of section 3 point at the same recipes and ratios).
6. The model's blind spots are reported, not hidden: `industry.warehouse` is never valued, and `industry.seed-capital` has a zero fluid-model gain for casual and prestige-later (their IP accumulates unspent, 18 to 49 IP by run 5).
7. Risk: the gates read the validator at revision 3 by string-replacing the revision; a future change of the JSON layout of `contentRevision` would need the regular expression updated (the gate fails closed: a read error is a diagnostic and the gate fails).

## 10. Reproduction

```
scripts/test-unity.ps1 -Suite EditMode -Category BalanceFull                       # full matrix, gates, budget
$env:IDLEFACTORY_WRITE_STRATEGY_BASELINE=1; scripts/test-unity.ps1 -Suite EditMode -Category BalanceFull   # also writes strategy-baseline-r3.md
$env:IDLEFACTORY_REGENERATE_BALANCE_TRACE=1; scripts/test-unity.ps1 -TestFile Assets/IdleFactory/Tests/EditMode/Balance/BalanceTraceTests.cs   # regenerates trace-r3.csv
scripts/test-unity.ps1 -TestFile Assets/IdleFactory/Tests/EditMode/Balance/BalanceTraceTests.cs         # fast gate (chain and Ore-only, offset 0, runs 1 and 2) and the golden
```
